humanities_role_explanation: HLE is a broad multi-subject expert exam (math, sciences, humanities) built to test frontier closed-ended academic knowledge. Humanities subjects (Classics, Art History, Musicology, Philosophy, Poetry, Linguistics) supply some items, but the benchmark does not target humanities disciplinary competence specifically; humanities is one category in the breakdown.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Questions are either text-only or text plus an accompanying image; around 14% require comprehending both text and an image. The remaining questions are text-only.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Closed-ended academic questions in two formats: exact-match short answers (76%) and multiple-choice (24%, five or more options). They test graduate-level knowledge and deep reasoning, with an emphasis on mathematics, and include some humanities items such as translating a Palmyrene inscription or identifying closed syllables in Biblical Hebrew. Models also state a confidence from 0-100%, and RMS calibration error is measured. Subjective interpretation and open-ended questions are explicitly prohibited, so open_ended_qa applies only to the short exact-match answers.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-subject benchmark of 2,500 questions across over a hundred subjects (math, humanities, natural sciences, etc.).

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, Grok 2, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking, o1, DeepSeek-R1, o3-mini (high).

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy (judged by o3-mini against the reference answer) and RMS calibration error; completion token counts are also reported.

summary: The paper introduces Humanity's Last Exam, a 2,500-question multi-modal benchmark of expert-written, closed-ended academic questions across over a hundred subjects, filtered so that frontier LLMs fail them. Questions go through LLM difficulty checks, two rounds of expert review, audits and a bug-bounty. Frontier models score low on accuracy and are poorly calibrated.
key_findings: Accuracy ranges from 2.7% (GPT-4o) to 13.4% (o3-mini high); RMS calibration error is 73-89% across all models, indicating confident wrong answers. Humanities accuracy (text-only) ranges from 1.0% to 10.4%. Reasoning models use far more completion tokens. Estimated expert disagreement rate is 15.4% on the public set (about 18% on a biology/chemistry/health subset).
facets_explanation: Questions and answers were written by nearly 1000 subject-expert contributors (mostly professors, researchers and graduate degree holders), each with a rationale. Reviewers holding graduate degrees checked them against rubrics. The rubric requires an 'objectively correct, univocal answer' and rejects subjective interpretation. Questions are meant to be non-searchable and to need specialized knowledge not in the prompt. Expert disagreement is estimated as an error rate to be reduced through audits and removals.
results_explanation: Table 1: O3-MINI (HIGH) reaches 13.4 accuracy (%) with 80 calibration error, the best result. Text-only vs full-dataset results (Tables 2 and 3) differ slightly for the same models, e.g. O1 7.8 text-only vs 8.0 full, so no meaningful gap in points is given. No human baseline score is reported, only an expert disagreement rate of 15.4%.
